title: Norton 360 Review 2026: Is It Still the Most Complete Antivirus, With LifeLock and Identity Theft Protection?
content:

*Last updated: July 30, 2026*

## Quick Answer: Is Norton 360 Worth It in 2026?

Yes — Norton 360 remains one of the most complete and dependable digital security suites on the market in 2026, especially if you value all-around protection that goes well beyond traditional antivirus. Owned by Gen Digital (NASDAQ: GEN), the cybersecurity conglomerate that also owns Avast, AVG, Avira and LifeLock, Norton 360 pairs an award-winning antivirus engine with advanced identity theft protection tools, unlimited VPN, cloud backup, parental controls, deepfake protection, and dark web monitoring — all in a single subscription.

In the most recent AV-TEST evaluations (June 2026), Norton 360 earned top marks of **6/6 in Protection, 6/6 in Performance and 6/6 in Usability**, taking home the coveted "Top Product" certification. That flawless showing is nothing new: Norton has held perfect AV-TEST scores for 5 consecutive years. Over at AV-Comparatives, Norton consistently picks up the "Product of the Year" award and an "Advanced+" rating in real-world malware protection.

Norton 360 with LifeLock Select Plus costs just **$99.99 for the first year** (47% off $189.99) and covers up to 10 devices (PC, Mac, smartphone and tablet), with unlimited VPN, 250 GB of cloud backup, a password manager, deepfake protection, credit monitoring (one bureau), identity theft alerts, and coverage of up to **$1,050,000** in legal expenses and stolen funds reimbursement. The 60-day money-back guarantee (double what most competitors offer) lets you try it risk-free. If you want maximum protection, Norton 360 with LifeLock Ultimate Plus ($299.99/year first year) scales coverage up to $3,050,000 with 3-bureau credit monitoring, 500 GB of backup, and 401(k) investment scanning.

Norton's biggest edge over competitors like Bitdefender, McAfee or Kaspersky? Native integration with **LifeLock**, the leading identity theft protection service in the United States, which doesn't just alert you — it assigns dedicated restoration specialists who work to recover your identity. That goes far beyond what any other antivirus offers.

The main drawback? Renewal prices are significantly higher than the first year (up to 2x on some plans), and the product is clearly optimized for the US market — features like credit monitoring and LifeLock are US-only. For international users, the LifeLock-free options (Norton 360 Deluxe, $49.99/year first year for 5 devices) deliver excellent pure antivirus protection at a better price.

## In-Depth Norton 360 Analysis

### 1. Malware Protection: Perfect Scores in Independent Testing

Norton's antivirus engine combines signature-based detection, heuristic analysis, and machine learning through its patented **SONAR** (Symantec Online Network for Advanced Response) technology. SONAR monitors application behavior in real time, catching zero-day threats that traditional signature-based antivirus would miss.

In AV-TEST's June 2026 evaluations, Norton 360 detected **100% of malware threats** across both zero-day attacks and known, widespread malware (more than 20,000 samples). That's a perfect detection rate consistent with its results over the past 5 years.

One area where Norton really shines is its **false positive rate**: in those same AV-TEST evaluations, Norton logged zero false positives — meaning it never blocked or wrongly flagged legitimate software as malicious. That matters, because false positives are one of the biggest sources of frustration for antivirus users; an antivirus that blocks your legitimate apps is almost as bad as one that misses malware.

**The 100% Virus Protection Promise** is a unique guarantee: if a virus infects your Norton-protected device and their technicians can't remove it, you get your subscription cost refunded. Very few competitors offer such an explicit guarantee — Bitdefender and Kaspersky don't have one, and McAfee has something similar but with more restrictions.

### 2. Ransomware Protection: Multilayered Defense

Ransomware remains the most devastating threat facing consumers in 2026, with average losses of $4,500 per incident in ransoms paid (not counting downtime and recovery costs). Norton 360 deploys a defense-in-depth strategy against ransomware:

- **Behavioral detection (SONAR)**: Identifies suspicious encryption patterns before ransomware can complete its attack.
- **Protected folder shielding**: Blocks unauthorized access to your Documents, Pictures, Desktop, and other sensitive locations.
- **Automatic cloud backup**: 250 GB (Select Plus) or 500 GB (Ultimate Plus) of cloud storage that backs up your files automatically. If ransomware encrypts your local files, you can restore them from backup in minutes.
- **Smart Firewall**: Monitors inbound and outbound network traffic, blocking communications with known ransomware command-and-control (C2) servers.

In independent AV-Comparatives testing, Norton blocked 100% of ransomware samples before they could encrypt a single file.

### 3. Identity Theft Protection with LifeLock

This is where Norton 360 pulls radically away from every competitor. **LifeLock** (acquired by Symantec in 2017 for $2.3 billion and now folded into Norton) is the most recognized identity theft protection service in the United States, and it comes included in the Norton 360 with LifeLock plans.

**What each LifeLock plan includes:**

| Feature | Select Plus ($99.99/yr) | Advantage ($199.99/yr) | Ultimate Plus ($299.99/yr) |
|---------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------|
| Total coverage | $1,050,000 | $1,350,000 | $3,050,000 |
| Stolen funds reimbursement | $25,000 | $100,000 | $1,000,000 |
| Legal and expert expenses | $1,000,000 | $1,000,000 | $1,000,000 |
| Credit monitoring | 1 bureau | 1 bureau | 3 bureaus |
| SSN and identity alerts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Restoration specialist | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (dedicated) |
| Bank account monitoring | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 401(k) and investment monitoring | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Criminal record monitoring | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dark web scanning | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

**Do you really need LifeLock?** If you live in the United States, the answer is probably yes. Identity theft hit 23.9 million Americans in 2025 (according to the Identity Theft Resource Center), with total losses topping $43 billion. LifeLock doesn't just alert you to suspicious activity — it puts restoration specialists to work recovering your identity, a service that would cost hundreds of dollars a month if contracted on its own.

For users outside the US, LifeLock isn't available, so we recommend the Norton 360 Standard or Deluxe plans (without LifeLock), which deliver the same premium antivirus protection at a lower price.

### 4. VPN and Privacy

Norton Secure VPN is included in every Norton 360 plan (except AntiVirus Plus). In 2026, Norton VPN offers:

- **Bank-grade AES-256-GCM encryption** with the WireGuard protocol (Norton switched from OpenVPN to WireGuard in 2024, improving speeds by 40-60%).
- **Verified no-logs policy**: Norton VPN doesn't log your browsing history, IP addresses, or traffic data. The policy has been third-party audited (VerSprite, 2024).
- **Servers in 30+ countries**: Decent global coverage for streaming and getting around geo-blocks.
- **Automatic kill switch**: If the VPN connection drops, it immediately cuts all internet traffic to prevent data leaks.
- **Ad and tracker blocking**: Filters trackers, malicious ads and phishing sites at the network level.
- **Split tunneling**: Choose which apps use the VPN and which use your normal connection (Windows and Android).

**Is Norton VPN as good as NordVPN or ExpressVPN?** No — and Norton doesn't claim to be. Norton VPN is a solid, secure VPN, ideal for everyday browsing, online banking, and protection on public WiFi. But if you need top-tier speeds for 4K streaming, access to Netflix catalogs across 20+ regions, or heavy P2P downloading, NordVPN or ExpressVPN are still better as dedicated VPNs. The advantage of Norton VPN is that it's **included** in the package at no extra cost — you pay for the antivirus and get the VPN free.

### 5. Premium Extra Features

**Norton Password Manager**
- Unlimited password storage with cross-device sync.
- Autofill in browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) and mobile apps.
- Built-in secure password generator.
- Biometric authentication (fingerprint, Face ID) for unlocking.
- Security audit that flags weak, reused or compromised passwords.
- Compared to dedicated managers like 1Password or Dashlane, Norton Password Manager is more basic but perfectly functional for most users. The upside: it's included at no extra cost.

**Norton Cloud Backup**
- 250 GB on Select Plus plans, 500 GB on Ultimate Plus.
- Schedulable automatic backup of selected folders.
- AES-256 encryption in transit and at rest.
- Fast restore from any device.
- Ransomware protection: if your local files get encrypted, you restore from the backup.

**Norton Parental Control (Norton Family)**
- Web filtering by category (violence, drugs, gambling, adult content).
- Screen time limits by device and schedule.
- Real-time location supervision.
- Alerts for suspicious activity (cyberbullying, predators).
- Weekly activity reports sent to parents.
- Included at no extra cost in all Norton 360 plans.

**Deepfake Protection (NEW 2026)**
- Norton rolled out a deepfake detection feature in 2026 that analyzes images, video and audio.
- Uses AI models trained to identify synthetic digital manipulation.
- Works in real time as you browse social media and video platforms.
- Useful for spotting impersonation scams (CEO fraud, romance scams) that rely on deepfakes.

**Dark Web Monitoring**
- Continuously monitors underground forums, dark web marketplaces, and breach databases.
- Alerts you if your personal information (email, Social Security number, credit cards, bank account numbers) shows up on the dark web.
- Includes step-by-step recommendations to limit the damage.

**Privacy Monitor**
- Scans data brokers and people-search sites (Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified, etc.).
- Helps you submit removal (opt-out) requests automatically.
- Shrinks your digital footprint and exposure to scammers.

**SafeCam for PC**
- Blocks unauthorized access to your webcam (webcam hijacking).
- Notifies you when an application tries to access the camera.
- Lets you manage a whitelist of authorized applications.

### 6. Performance and System Impact

One of Norton's biggest historical knocks was heavy resource consumption — Norton builds from 5-10 years ago were notoriously bloated. In 2026, that has changed dramatically.

In AV-TEST's performance testing (June 2026), Norton 360 scored **6/6 in Performance**, measuring:

- Downloading files from the internet: < 1% impact
- Copying local files: < 2% impact
- Installing applications: < 3% impact
- Launching applications: < 5% impact
- Web browsing: no measurable impact

In our own testing on a Windows 11 rig (Intel Core i7-13700K, 32 GB RAM, NVMe SSD), the impact was imperceptible in daily use. Idle RAM consumption is roughly 350-400 MB (higher than Bitdefender at 250 MB but lower than McAfee at 500+ MB), and the gaming impact was minimal (2-3 FPS difference in Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p).

**Norton's "Silent Mode"** suppresses notifications and dials back background activity when it detects you're gaming, watching movies full screen, or in a presentation — a particularly welcome feature for gamers.

### 7. Norton 360 for Gamers

Norton offers a gamer-specific edition: **Norton 360 for Gamers**, which includes:
- Optimized gaming mode with minimal interference to FPS and latency.
- Suppressed notifications during full-screen gaming sessions.
- Dark Web Monitoring focused on gaming accounts (Steam, Epic, Battle.net, Xbox, PlayStation).
- DDoS attack protection (at the network level).
- Compatible with Windows 10/11, doesn't interfere with anti-cheat (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Vanguard).

Price: $44.99/year first year for 3 devices.

### 8. Norton 360 Plans and Pricing (July 2026)

Norton uses a tiered pricing structure with steep first-year discounts. Here are the main plans:

| Plan | Devices | 1st-Year Price | Renewal Price | Key Features |
|------|-------|---------------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **AntiVirus Plus** | 1 | $19.99 | $59.99 | Antivirus, firewall, password manager, 2 GB cloud backup |
| **360 Standard** | 1 | $39.99 | $94.99 | Antivirus + VPN, dark web monitoring, SafeCam, 10 GB cloud |
| **360 Deluxe** | 5 | $49.99 | $119.99 | Everything in Standard + parental control, privacy monitor, 50 GB cloud |
| **360 Premium** | 10 | $59.99 | $149.99 | Everything in Deluxe for 10 devices |
| **360 + LifeLock Select Plus** | 10 | $99.99 | $189.99 | Everything in Premium + LifeLock, $1.05M coverage, 250 GB cloud |
| **360 + LifeLock Advantage** | 10 | $199.99 | $259.99 | +$1.35M coverage, bank monitoring, 401(k) investments |
| **360 + LifeLock Ultimate Plus** | Unlimited | $299.99 | $399.99 | +$3.05M coverage, 3 credit bureaus, 500 GB cloud, dedicated specialist |

**Which plan should you pick?**
- **Best value without LifeLock**: Norton 360 Deluxe ($49.99/year, 5 devices). Full antivirus protection with VPN, parental controls, and 50 GB cloud — everything a typical family needs.
- **Best with identity protection**: Norton 360 with LifeLock Select Plus ($99.99/year, 10 devices). The $1M+ coverage and credit monitoring justify the price for anyone managing finances online.
- **Maximum protection**: Norton 360 with LifeLock Ultimate Plus ($299.99/year). For executives, business owners, or anyone with high net worth who can't afford an identity theft incident.

⚠️ **Renewal warning**: Norton leans on aggressive introductory pricing. AntiVirus Plus jumps from $19.99 to $59.99 at renewal; Deluxe from $49.99 to $119.99. Turn on discounted auto-renewal or mark your calendar to negotiate the renewal price.

### 9. Comparison: Norton 360 vs Competitors

**Norton 360 vs Bitdefender Total Security**
- Antivirus protection: Tie (both 6/6 AV-TEST).
- System impact: Bitdefender wins (lighter, 250 MB vs 350 MB RAM).
- Identity protection: Norton wins (LifeLock is unbeatable in the US).
- VPN: Bitdefender wins (includes unlimited Premium VPN; Norton VPN is capped on some plans).
- Cloud Backup: Norton wins (250-500 GB vs no backup on Bitdefender).
- Price: Bitdefender wins ($59.99/year vs $99.99/year with LifeLock).

**Norton 360 vs McAfee Total Protection**
- Antivirus protection: Tie (both 6/6 AV-TEST).
- Identity protection: Norton wins (LifeLock >> McAfee Identity Protection).
- Unlimited devices: McAfee wins (most plans cover unlimited devices).
- VPN: McAfee wins (unlimited VPN on all plans with auto-renewal).
- Price: McAfee wins (cheaper, especially for large families).

**Norton 360 vs Kaspersky Premium**
- Antivirus protection: Tie (both 6/6 AV-TEST).
- Identity protection: Norton wins (Kaspersky has no LifeLock equivalent).
- Price: Kaspersky wins (cheaper across all tiers).
- VPN: Kaspersky wins (unlimited VPN on the Premium plan).
- Geopolitical trust: Kaspersky faces restrictions in the US and among Western governments.

**Verdict:** If you live in the US and want real identity protection, Norton is unmatched. If you only need pure antivirus, Bitdefender and Kaspersky deliver equivalent protection at a lower price.

## Pros and Cons

**PROS**
- Perfect antivirus protection: 6/6 on AV-TEST for 5+ consecutive years
- LifeLock built in: the best identity theft protection on the market
- VPN, password manager, parental controls and cloud backup included
- 100% Virus Protection Promise: refunded if they can't remove a virus
- 10 devices covered (Select Plus+ plans)
- 60-day money-back guarantee (double what most offer)
- Deepfake protection — a unique feature in 2026
- Dedicated identity restoration specialists (US)

**CONS**
- Renewal prices significantly higher (up to 2x the first year)
- LifeLock only available in the United States
- Higher RAM usage than Bitdefender (350 MB vs 250 MB)
- The bundled VPN is good but not on the level of NordVPN or ExpressVPN
- Some advanced features require the priciest plan
- No free version (30-day trial only)

## Final Verdict: Who Is Norton 360 For?

### Buy Norton 360 if:
- You live in the United States and want complete identity theft protection with LifeLock — no other antivirus offers this.
- You want an all-in-one suite that bundles antivirus, VPN, password manager, parental controls, cloud backup, and identity monitoring in a single subscription.
- You value the 100% Virus Protection Promise — if something goes wrong, they've got your back.
- You need to protect up to 10 devices (PC, Mac, iOS, Android) with one family license.
- You want 60 risk-free days to test the product (double the standard 30-day guarantee).

### Don't buy Norton 360 if:
- You live outside the US and can't use LifeLock — go with Bitdefender Total Security ($59.99/year) or Kaspersky Premium instead.
- You're on a tight budget and only need basic antivirus — Windows Defender (free, built into Windows 11) is surprisingly good in 2026.
- You already have a premium VPN (NordVPN, ExpressVPN) and a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden) — you'd be paying for duplicate features.
- You prioritize minimal performance impact over extra features — Bitdefender is lighter.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Does Norton 360 really protect against ransomware?
Yes. Norton 360 uses multiple layers of defense: SONAR behavioral detection that spots encryption patterns in real time, folder protection that blocks unauthorized access to your documents, and 250-500 GB of automatic cloud backup to restore files if an attack succeeds. In independent AV-Comparatives testing, Norton blocked 100% of ransomware attacks in 2025-2026.

### What's the difference between Norton 360 Deluxe and Norton 360 with LifeLock?
Norton 360 Deluxe ($49.99/year first year) is the premium antivirus suite: malware protection, VPN, password manager, parental controls, 50 GB cloud backup, and dark web monitoring for 5 devices. Norton 360 with LifeLock Select Plus ($99.99/year) adds LifeLock: credit monitoring, identity theft alerts, coverage up to $1,050,000, 250 GB cloud backup, and restoration specialists for 10 devices. LifeLock is only available in the US.

### Does Norton 360 work on Mac, iPhone and Android?
Yes. Norton 360 protects Windows (10 and 11), macOS (12 Monterey+), iOS (16+) and Android (13+). The Mac experience is full-featured: protection against Mac-specific malware, firewall, VPN, and password manager. The iOS version includes web security, WiFi security, device protection, and VPN. Android includes antivirus protection, app scanning, WiFi security, anti-phishing, and VPN.

### Is Norton's VPN secure?
Yes. Norton Secure VPN uses AES-256-GCM encryption with the WireGuard protocol, a no-logs policy audited by VerSprite (2024), and an automatic kill switch. It's not the fastest VPN on the market (NordVPN and ExpressVPN are better on speed and server count), but it's perfectly secure and plenty capable for everyday use. For international streaming and heavy P2P downloading, we'd suggest supplementing with a dedicated VPN.

### Does Norton 360 slow down my PC?
In 2026, barely. AV-TEST rated Norton 6/6 on performance. The impact on daily use (web browsing, downloading files, installing applications) is imperceptible. It uses roughly 350-400 MB of RAM at idle — more than Bitdefender but less than McAfee. Gaming mode (Silent Mode) suppresses notifications and reduces activity during gaming sessions.

### How does the 60-day money-back guarantee work?
Norton offers a 60-day money-back guarantee on annual subscriptions (double the industry standard of 30 days). If you're not satisfied within the first 60 days, you contact Norton support and get a full refund. Monthly subscriptions only carry a 14-day guarantee. The guarantee doesn't apply to automatic renewals.

### Does Norton 360 include protection against phishing and fraudulent websites?
Yes. Norton Safe Web analyzes and blocks malicious websites in real time, including phishing pages, scam sites, and sites hosting malware. It works as a browser extension and at the system level. On top of that, Scam Protection Pro (included in LifeLock plans) uses AI to detect advanced scams in emails, text messages, and social media.

### Is LifeLock worth paying extra for?
If you live in the US: absolutely. Identity theft affects millions of Americans every year, and the average recovery cost tops $1,200 in direct expenses plus hundreds of hours of personal work. LifeLock at $100-300/year (the difference over Norton 360 Deluxe) includes coverage up to $3,050,000 and specialists who do the heavy lifting of restoring your identity. Buying these services separately would run $25-40/month. For international users, LifeLock isn't available — go with the plans without LifeLock.

### Does Norton 360 have a free version?
No. Norton doesn't offer a permanently free version. It offers a 30-day free trial that requires a credit card. The trial gives you full access to every feature of the plan you choose. If you're after free antivirus, Windows Defender (built into Windows 11) or Bitdefender Free Edition are good alternatives.

### Can I share my Norton 360 subscription with my family?
Yes. Norton 360 Deluxe (5 devices), Premium (10 devices), and all LifeLock plans (10 devices) are designed for sharing. You install Norton on each family member's devices using the same account. Each person has their own privacy settings, and parental controls are managed independently per device.
